chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'From the middle of what you feed your families,' he said: 'It is as it becomes; indeed, there will be in the household some who eat more than a mudd and some who eat less than a mudd, so it is between that. And if you wish, you provide them with side dishes (udm). The side dish is: its lowest is salt, its middle is oil and vinegar, and its highest is meat.'

key_terms.أُدْمًا: Side dishes or condiments served with the main meal
key_terms.الْمُدِّ: A standard unit of volume measurement for dry food

ai.seo_question: What does 'middle of what you feed your families' mean for expiation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the Quranic term 'middle' (awsat) not as a fixed quantity but as a spectrum of quality, ranging from basic salt to premium meat, thereby allowing flexibility based on household means. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on practicality and economic capacity in fulfilling religious obligations, ensuring that expiation remains accessible to all social classes.
